sections.heading: SHM fundamentals
bullets: SHM: acceleration a = −ω²x — restoring force proportional to displacement, opposite in direction.
x(t) = A cos(ωt + φ); v = −Aω sin(ωt+φ); a = −Aω² cos(ωt+φ).
Energy shuttles between ½kx² and ½mv²; total E = ½mω²A² is constant.
Spring-mass: ω = √(k/m); simple pendulum (small angle): ω = √(g/L), T = 2π√(L/g).

sections.heading: Damped & driven oscillations
bullets: Damping adds −bv: amplitude decays as e^{−bt/2m}; underdamped oscillates, overdamped creeps.
Resonance: driving at ω ≈ ω₀ maximises amplitude (Q factor = ω₀/broadness).
Phase: displacement lags driving force near resonance by π/2.

sections.heading: Waves
bullets: v = fλ; transverse (string, light) vs longitudinal (sound).
y = A sin(kx − ωt), k = 2π/λ, ω = 2πf; wave equation ∂²y/∂x² = (1/v²)∂²y/∂t².
Superposition → interference; standing waves when two opposite waves lock: fₙ = n·v/2L (string fixed both ends).
Doppler: f′ = f(v ± vₒ)/(v ∓ vₛ) — approach positive, recede negative (for observer still).

questions.prompt: A spring-mass system has k = 200 N/m and m = 0.5 kg. Find ω and T.
In SHM, where is kinetic energy maximum and potential energy maximum?
questions.answer: KE max at mean position (x=0); PE max at extreme (x=±A)
solution: KE = ½mω²(A² − x²) ⇒ max when x = 0.

questions.prompt: A string 1.5 m long, fixed at both ends, vibrates in 3 loops at 120 Hz. Find wave speed.
solution: 3 loops ⇒ the string holds three half-wavelengths: L = 3·(λ/2).

questions.prompt: A 440 Hz source moves toward you at 30 m/s (v_sound = 340 m/s). Apparent frequency?

sections.heading: Electrostatics
bullets: Coulomb: F = q₁q₂/(4πε₀r²); field of point charge E = q/(4πε₀r²).
Gauss: ∮E·dA = Q_enc/ε₀ — pick symmetry (plane, sphere, cylinder) before integrating.
Potential V = −∫E·dl; for point charge V = q/(4πε₀r); equipotential surfaces ⊥ field lines.
capacitor energy U = ½CV²; energy density u = ½ε₀E².

sections.heading: Magnetostatics
bullets: Biot–Savart for wires/loops; long straight wire B = μ₀I/(2πr).
Ampère: ∮B·dl = μ₀I_enc — solenoid interior B = μ₀nI uniform.
Lorentz force F = q(v × B) — circle radius r = mv/(qB), cyclotron frequency f = qB/(2πm).

sections.heading: Faraday, Maxwell & EM waves
bullets: Faraday: ε = −dΦ_B/dt (Lenz's law gives the minus sign — induced effects oppose change).
Maxwell's four equations complete the set: displacement current ε₀dΦ_E/dt adds the missing term.
EM waves in vacuum: c = 1/√(μ₀ε₀) ≈ 3×10⁸ m/s; E, B and propagation mutually ⊥.
Wave impedance Z₀ = E/B = c; intensity ∝ E².

questions.prompt: Electric field at distance r from an infinitely long charged wire with linear density λ?
solution: Cylindrical Gaussian surface of radius r, length L.

questions.prompt: A 10-turn coil of radius 5 cm carries 2 A. Approximate B at its centre.
solution: Centre of current loop: B = μ₀NI/(2R).

questions.prompt: A 0.5 H inductor sees current change from 2 A to 5 A in 4 ms. Induced emf?
solution: Lenz's law: the emf opposes the current increase.

questions.prompt: In a uniform B = 0.1 T, an electron (v = 10⁶ m/s ⊥ B) moves in a circle. Find radius.
solution: r = mv/(qB) with m = 9.11×10⁻³¹ kg, q = 1.6×10⁻¹⁹ C.

sections.heading: Ray optics
bullets: Mirror equation 1/f = 1/v + 1/u (sign convention: real-is-positive or Cartesian — pick one and stick to it).
Refraction: n₁ sinθ₁ = n₂ sinθ₂; apparent depth = real depth × (n₂/n₁).
Critical angle θc = sin⁻¹(n₂/n₁) → total internal reflection when going dense → rare.
Lens maker: 1/f = (n−1)(1/R₁ − 1/R₂); thin-lens combination 1/F = Σ1/fᵢ.

sections.heading: Interference
bullets: Young's double slit: fringe width β = λD/d — bright and dark alternate with path difference mλ / (m+½)λ.
Thin films: reflected phase shift of π at denser medium; colour depends on 2nt = (m+½)λ (reflected).
Coherent sources required — splitting one source is the classic trick.

sections.heading: Diffraction & instruments
bullets: Single slit minima: a sinθ = mλ; central max width = 2λD/a (twice the double-slit fringe).
Resolving power: Rayleigh criterion θ = 1.22 λ/D for circular aperture.
Grating: d sinθ = mλ — more slits ⇒ sharper, brighter principal maxima.

questions.prompt: An object 10 cm tall is 30 cm from a concave mirror of f = −15 cm. Find image distance.
Double slit: d = 0.5 mm, D = 1 m, λ = 600 nm. Fringe width?
Critical angle for glass (n = 1.5) to air?
Single slit of width 0.2 mm: first diffraction minimum at what angle for λ = 500 nm?

sections.heading: Quantum foundations
bullets: Planck: E = hν; photon momentum p = h/λ — light behaves as particles in photoelectric effect.
de Broglie: λ = h/(mv) — every particle has a wave; electron in 1 V: λ ≈ 1.2 nm.
Heisenberg: Δx·Δp ≥ ħ/2 — measurement disturbs the system.
Schrödinger equation gives ψ; |ψ|² is probability density — quantisation appears from boundary conditions.

sections.heading: Quantum in a box & tunnelling
bullets: Particle in 1-D box: Eₙ = n²h²/(8mL²) — energy gaps shrink as L grows.
Tunnelling probability drops exponentially with barrier width — basis of tunnel diode & STM.
Photoelectric equation: KEmax = hν − φ — threshold frequency ν₀ = φ/h.

sections.heading: Semiconductors
bullets: Intrinsic: nᵢ² = n·p; doping → n-type (donors) or p-type (acceptors).
p-n junction: depletion region, barrier ≈ 0.7 V for Si; forward bias conducts, reverse blocks.
Zener breakdown (heavily doped, sharp) vs avalanche (gradual, impact ionisation).
Diode equations: I = Iₛ(e^{V/ηV_T} − 1); half/full rectifiers convert AC → pulsating DC (filtered with C).

questions.prompt: Light of λ = 400 nm hits a metal with φ = 2.0 eV. Find KEmax.
Electron accelerated through 100 V: de Broglie wavelength?
solution: λ = 1.226/√100 = 0.1226 nm ≈ 0.123 nm — comparable to crystal spacing ⇒ XRD works.

questions.prompt: In a box of length L = 1 nm, ground-state electron energy scale?
Doping silicon with phosphorus creates which carrier type and why?
questions.answer: n-type — phosphorus has 5 valence electrons (extra free electron)
solution: Four bonds form; the fifth electron is loosely bound → donated to conduction band.
Majority carriers = electrons; holes remain minority.
